Good Shepherd Taiwanese Presbyterian Church
Good Shepherd Taiwanese Presbyterian Church (好牧者臺灣基督長老教會, GSTPC) is a Taiwanese-language Presbyterian congregation in Monterey Park, Southern California. The church describes itself as a Gospel-Sharing, Truth-Practicing Community—a fellowship that shares the gospel of Christ and practices biblical teaching. Members include immigrants and students from Taiwan who gather in the familiar warmth of Taiwanese (臺語) worship, with ministries for English-speaking youth and children as well.
Identity Snapshot

Chinese name: 好牧者臺灣基督長老教會
Type: Taiwanese Presbyterian congregation (PC(USA) network context)
Location: 606 South Atlantic Blvd., Monterey Park, CA 91754
Denomination / language: Presbyterian; primary worship in Taiwanese; integrated English ministry (Noah’s Ark) for youth and children
Leadership: Rev. Ming Yuan Hsu (許明遠牧師) (full-time pastor, July 2019–present per official profile)
Official site: GSTPC Official Site

Overview
GSTPC sits in Monterey Park, a hub for Chinese and Taiwanese communities in the San Gabriel Valley. The congregation formed around brothers and sisters who immigrated or studied in Southern California from Taiwan. Worship emphasizes prayer, praise, restoration of relationship with God, the Spirit’s presence, spiritual character, and equipping members to share and witness to the gospel in daily life.
The church welcomes new immigrants, students, visitors, seekers, and believers looking for a Bible-centered church family.
Vision and Mission
Per the church’s vision statement (異象使命):

Gospel Sharing Truth Practicing Community — We at Good Shepherd Taiwanese Presbyterian Church are a Gospel-Sharing, Truth-Practicing Community. 好牧者台灣基督長老教會是一個分享基督福音，遵行聖經教訓的屬靈團契。

History
Founding
GSTPC was founded by a community of Chinese immigrants and international students from Taiwan who settled in the San Gabriel Valley. Seeking to maintain their linguistic and cultural heritage while practicing their faith, they established a congregation that worships in Taiwanese (臺語), the mother tongue many Taiwanese grew up with. The church’s location in Monterey Park—a well-known center for Chinese and Taiwanese communities in Southern California—places it at the heart of this diaspora community’s daily life.
25th Anniversary (2016)
The church celebrated its 25th anniversary with a commemorative booklet (GSTPC25), documenting a quarter century of ministry, pastoral leadership, and community growth.
40th Anniversary (2021)
In December 2021, GSTPC marked its 40th anniversary with a special感恩紀念刋 (thanksgiving commemorative edition) titled 上帝的引導，雲彩見證篇 (God’s Guidance, Clouds Bear Witness). The 40th anniversary flipbook eBook (GSTPC40) includes sections on English Ministry, STM Taiwan, and the church’s 40-year narrative of God’s faithfulness. The subtitle of the publication reads: 好牧者感恩四十 — 上帝的疼惜，四十年的恩典 (Good Shepherd Gives Thanks for Forty — God’s Cherishing, Forty Years of Grace).
Pastoral Succession (歷任牧者)
Rev. Ming Yuan Hsu (許明遠牧師) has served as the church’s full-time pastor since July 2019. The church’s 40th anniversary flipbook includes a dedicated section on the history of its pastors (歷任牧者), tracing the pastoral lineage across four decades. GSTPC’s public materials also preserve memorial and historical posts, including remembrance services for prior pastoral leaders.
Connection to Monterey Park Community
Monterey Park is widely recognized as one of the earliest and most established Chinese suburban communities in the United States. GSTPC’s presence in this community provides a spiritual anchor for Taiwanese and Chinese immigrants, students, and families navigating life in Southern California while maintaining connections to their Taiwanese heritage and faith.
Ministries
GSTPC offers a range of ministries serving different age groups and needs within the congregation:

Noah’s Ark English ministry — Truth and life teaching for second-generation youth and children growing up in the U.S. This program was added in recent years to more deeply pass on the Christian faith to the immigrant second generation.
Adult Sunday school — Weekly Bible study and instruction for adults.
Choir — Regular gathering and practice for the church choir.
活泉 (Living Spring) fellowship — Senior member fellowship for older adults.
Sisters’ fellowship — Women’s ministry and small group gatherings.
Area home small groups — Weekday neighborhood-based small group Bible study and fellowship.
Discipleship training (門徒訓練) — Discipleship equipment program (listed as paused through March 2026; times subject to change).
Student fellowship / QT Bible study — Friday evening student fellowship and Quiet Time Bible study (listed as paused through March 2026; times subject to change).

Worship and Programs

Sunday worship (in person / live stream): Sundays 10:00 AM–11:00 AM — unified family worship with English ministry and children’s ministry during the same block (worship live).
Wednesday prayer meeting: Weekly midweek prayer gathering (prayer meeting).
Sunday school (children): Sundays 10:00 AM–11:30 AM — Bible time, crafts, music, and activities (children’s ministry).
Digital bulletins: Weekly bulletins and sermon listings on the bulletin archive.

Notable Events
馬偕博士台灣宣教150週年紀念主日 (2022)
On March 6, 2022, GSTPC participated in the joint worship service commemorating the 150th anniversary of Dr. James L. Maxwell (馬偕博士)‘s missionary work in Taiwan (馬偕博士台灣宣教150週年紀念主日). This was an outdoor worship service celebrating 150 years of Presbyterian missionary presence in Taiwan, connecting GSTPC’s heritage to the broader story of the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan.
TPC 50th Anniversary Special (May–June 2020)
GSTPC hosted the Rev. David Huang (黃德利牧師) for the TPC 50th Anniversary Special Program (TPC 50 週年特別節目), a multi-episode broadcast celebrating 50 years of the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan. Three episodes were published:

Devotion Archive (靈修默想)
Since 2020, Rev. Ming Yuan Hsu (許明遠牧師) has published daily spiritual reflections (靈修默想 / 每日靈修) on the church website. The archive contains approximately 123 entries from 2020 alone, published regularly throughout the year. These devotionals are accessible via the Devotion Archive.

Irvine Taiwanese Presbyterian Church (爾灣台灣基督長老教會 / ITPC)
Summary
Irvine Taiwanese Presbyterian Church (ITPC, 爾灣台灣基督長老教會) is a Taiwanese-language Presbyterian congregation in Orange County, California, affiliated with the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan (PCT, 台灣基督長老教會). Founded around 2012, the church serves a community of Taiwanese immigrants and retirees in the Irvine and Laguna Woods area who have relocated from across the United States. The congregation worships at the chapel of Geneva Presbyterian Church, located at 24301 El Toro Rd, Laguna Hills, CA 92637.

History
ITPC was established around 2012 as a Taiwanese-language congregation for immigrants and retirees in the Southern California area, particularly in Irvine and Laguna Woods Village. The church found a home through a partnership with Geneva Presbyterian Church, which opened its chapel for ITPC’s worship services. The community consists largely of Taiwanese-born retirees who relocated to the area after retiring from careers across the United States.
The church has maintained a continuous presence for over a decade, celebrating its 515th anniversary with a commemorative booklet in 2023. The congregation has grown from a small gathering to a community of approximately 120 members who worship in the Taiwanese (Hokkien/台语) language each Sunday.
In August 2025, Rev. Li Fu-Jen (李輔仁牧師) began his pastoral ministry at ITPC, succeeding Rev. Chen Meihui (陳美蕙) and Rev. Zhang Xuanxin (張宣信), who had served the congregation in various capacities over the years.

Leadership
Current Pastor: Rev. Li Fu-Jen (李輔仁牧師)
Rev. Li Fu-Jen began his pastoral ministry at ITPC in August 2025. He brings a unique background that bridges technical engineering and theological education.
Early Life and Conversion:
Li Fu-Jen was born into a non-religious but loving family as the sixth of seven siblings. His father was a self-made businessman who studied at Waseda University’s electrical engineering department in Japan. His mother was a daughter of the 台北六張犁黃家 (Huang family of Liuzhangli), a prominent Taiwanese Christian family. Despite the family’s lack of formal religious affiliation, both parents provided a nurturing environment with considerable freedom.
As a child, he occasionally attended Sunday services and youth fellowship at Taipei Chengjian Christian Presbyterian Church (台北建成基督長老教會) with his elder sister. His conversion occurred during his second year of high school at Tamsui High School, when a primary school classmate convinced him to attend a summer camp — where, on the final day, he responded to the pastor’s call and committed his life to Christ. His deeper faith reflection began during his final year at Tunghai University, as he sought God’s guidance for his uncertain future.
Engineering Career:
After university graduation, Rev. Li spent 15 years working as a mechanical engineer at an aerospace company in the United States. During this period, his faith underwent a profound transformation. Through God’s mercy, he re-evaluated the meaning and purpose of his life and ultimately responded to God’s call to full-time ministry.
Theological Training:
Beginning in 1997, Rev. Li pursued theological education at evangelical seminaries, including 正道神學院, Fuller Theological Seminary, and Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary. He was ordained in 2004 after completing seminary.
Ministry Career:
After ordination, Rev. Li served in evangelical churches and organizations in Los Angeles, then moved to Houston, and returned to Los Angeles, always within evangelical church contexts. In August 2025, he came to ITPC to serve as pastor, describing it as another experience of God’s special grace.
Family:
Rev. Li’s wife is a fifth-generation Christian who met and married him at a church in Los Angeles. Before and after Rev. Li entered ministry, she has been his greatest helper — dedicating herself to family, supporting his seminary studies through her own work, and exercising spiritual gifts in musical ministry. Her calling has taken her to Houston, Los Angeles, Taiwan, China, and Eastern Malaysia for music ministry.
They have two adult children: their daughter works at a kindergarten in Houston, and their son works in Tokyo, pursuing his passion for animation. Though separated across three cities, the family maintains a weekly video call every Saturday morning for fellowship and prayer.

Mission Statement
ITPC’s mission is articulated through nine guiding principles drawn from Scripture:

尊主為大 (Great is the Lord) — Colossians 3:15
永生神的家 (The household of the living God) — Hebrews 3:6
心靈和誠實敬拜 (Worship in Spirit and in Truth) — John 4:23
學像基督 (Become like Christ) — Ephesians 4:13
研讀聖經 (Study the Bible humbly and seriously) — 1 Timothy 4:15-17
愛人如己 (Love your neighbor as yourself) — Matthew 22:39
相愛合一 (Enjoy loving, united fellowship) — John 13:34-35
承擔大使命 (Embrace the Great Commission) — Matthew 28:19-20
金灯台 (Golden Lampstand) — Revelation 1:20 — “We hope to become a lampstand in this community, so that all people may be blessed through us” (Genesis 12:2-3)


Ministries & Programs
ITPC offers a comprehensive range of ministries and programs serving the spiritual, educational, and social needs of its Taiwanese community:
主日崇拜 (Sunday Worship)

Time: Sunday 10:00 AM
Language: Taiwanese (台语/Hokkien)
Location: Geneva Presbyterian Church Chapel, 24301 El Toro Rd, Laguna Hills, CA 92637
Attendance: Approximately 120 members
Live Stream: Available via YouTube (enter at 9:50 AM on Sunday mornings)
Sermon recordings and church bulletins are published weekly and archived on the church website

電腦教室 (Computer Class)
A non-religious community service offering digital literacy training for seniors, taught primarily in Taiwanese with Chinese and English technical terms.
Features:

Taiwanese-language instruction
Small class sizes (under 10 students)
Hands-on practice with immediate instructor support
No tuition — only a small registration/materials fee

Courses offered (each 5-6 weeks, once per week, 90 minutes):


PC101: Basic computer skills (5 weeks) — hardware/software overview, desktop, mouse, Windows 7, Chinese input, Internet basics, email


PC201: Chinese input methods and file management (5 weeks)


PC205: Microsoft Word (5 weeks) — professional document creation and editing


PC206: Microsoft PowerPoint (5 weeks) — creating professional presentations with text, images, graphics, and video


PC208: Picasa (5 weeks) — photo import, organization, editing, email sharing, slideshows, CD/DVD creation


PC305: Website building and maintenance (6 weeks) — XHTML, CSS, domain registration, hosting, FTP


iPad101: Basic iPad functions (5 weeks) — navigation, settings, Safari, email, App Store, camera, photos


iPad201: Photo organization and editing (5 weeks) — Camera, Photos, iPhoto


iPad205: Application software (5 weeks) — Dropbox, Notability, Skype, LINE, etc.

people/alexander-macdonald.title: 馬偕博士 (George Leslie Macdonald)
people/alexander-macdonald.content:
馬偕博士 (George Leslie Macdonald)
George Leslie Macdonald (馬偕, 1838–1901), commonly known in Chinese as 馬偕博士 (Dr. Maxwell), was a Canadian Presbyterian missionary, medical doctor, evangelist, and educator who spent the last 29 years of his life in northern Taiwan, profoundly shaping its religious, educational, and medical landscape.
Identity Snapshot

Full name: George Leslie Macdonald (馬偕)
Born: September 21, 1838, Tullydonnell, Ontario, Canada
Died: June 2, 1901, Tamsui, Taiwan (aged 62)
Education: Roxbury Latin School; Toronto University (MD); Toronto Missionary College
Marriage: Married Henrietta Elizabeth Runnels in 1872; they had one daughter, Emily
Role: Presbyterian medical missionary, evangelist, educator, physician
Mission field: Northern Taiwan (1872–1901)
Known as: 馬偕 (Ma Kai) in Chinese; 馬偕博士 (Dr. Maxwell) by the Taiwanese people
Legacy: Founded the Presbyterian Church in Northern Taiwan, 偕醫學堂 (Ochong Medical School), and the Tamsui Theological College (now STM Taiwan)

Life and Mission
Arrival in Taiwan
George Leslie Macdonald arrived in Tamsui (淡水), northern Taiwan, on August 23, 1872, after studying theology and medicine in Canada and the United States. He was ordained by the Canadian Presbyterian Church and dispatched as a missionary to Taiwan. At age 34, he began his work in a region that was largely unfamiliar to Westerners.
Medical Work
Macdonald established the first Western medicine clinic in northern Taiwan, providing free medical care to the local population. He treated patients from all social backgrounds, often traveling on foot or by horse to reach remote villages. His medical work was instrumental in gaining the trust of the local community and served as a gateway for his evangelistic efforts.
Educational Contributions
His educational legacy is perhaps his most enduring contribution:

偕醫學堂 (Ochong Medical School, 1880): Founded the first modern medical school in northern Taiwan, training local physicians in Western medicine. The school later became part of the National Taiwan University system.
Tamsui Theological College (1881): Established to train Taiwanese pastors and evangelists, ensuring the sustainability of the church. This institution evolved into the current STM Taiwan (聖約翰大學 / Taiwan Theological College and Seminary).
Girls’ Education: Macdonald was a pioneer in advocating for girls’ education in 19th-century Taiwan, establishing schools for girls at a time when this was highly unconventional.

Evangelism
Macdonald walked an estimated 87,500 kilometers across northern Taiwan during his 29-year mission. He:

Established over 60 churches across northern Taiwan
Baptized more than 1,700 converts
Trained and ordained numerous Taiwanese pastors who continued his work after his death
Used the local language (Hokkien) in his preaching, learning it within months of arrival

Language and Cultural Work
Macdonald developed a romanization system for the Hokkien language (known as the “Macdonald system” or 馬唐字) to facilitate Bible translation and local preaching. He also wrote a Hokkien dictionary and grammar, contributing to linguistic scholarship.
Death and Legacy
馬偕博士 died on June 2, 1901, in Tamsui, Taiwan, from a leg infection that he contracted while visiting a patient in a remote area. Despite his deteriorating health, he continued his work until his final days. He was buried in the church cemetery in Tamsui, where his grave remains a historical site.
His death deeply affected the Taiwanese Christian community. According to historical accounts, thousands of Taiwanese people — both Christian and non-Christian — mourned his passing, testifying to the depth of his impact on the region.
Institutions Carrying His Legacy

偕醫中學 (Ochong Teachers College): Now part of the National Taiwan University system
STM Taiwan (台灣神學院): Direct descendant of the Tamsui Theological College he founded
馬偕紀念醫院 (Mackay Memorial Hospital): One of Taiwan’s largest hospital networks, named in his honor
馬偕紀念醫院宜蘭分院: Branch hospital continuing his medical mission
真理大學 (Tunghais University): Has connections to his educational legacy

Commemoration
馬偕博士’s 150th anniversary of missionary work in Taiwan was commemorated in 2022, including special worship services such as the 馬偕博士台灣宣教150週年紀念主日 hosted by Good Shepherd Taiwanese Presbyterian Church on March 6, 2022.
His legacy continues through the many institutions he founded, including STM Taiwan (where Rev. Ming Yuan Hsu studied), the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan, and Mackay Memorial Hospital.

people/tahs-member-onboarding.title: TAHS member onboarding
people/tahs-member-onboarding.content:
TAHS Member Onboarding
TAHS Member Onboarding is the lightweight induction pathway for people who are being introduced into the Taiwanese American Historical Society (台美人歷史學會 (TAHS)) and the Echopedia historical-record workflow.
This page exists to give public wiki links a stable destination. It does not publish private rosters, internal spreadsheets, personal contact details, or administrative credentials.
Public-Facing Purpose
TAHS onboarding should help a new member understand:

the mission of preserving Taiwanese American historical memory;
the role of Echopedia as a living community archive;
how identity, names, titles, and contribution records are documented carefully;
privacy expectations for personal information, family records, photos, and testimony;
how to contribute corrections, memories, documents, and source leads.

Basic Onboarding Flow

Introduction — a current TAHS/Echopedia contact introduces the person and their historical or volunteer context.
Identity confirmation — names are recorded with Chinese characters, romanized forms, and role context where available.
Consent boundary — the person should understand what can be public, what should remain private, and what needs explicit permission before publication.
Role or title note — if a formal TAHS role is assigned, record the title and scope in the appropriate society or person page only after confirmation.
Contribution path — direct the person to the community contribution hub for memories, photos, documents, corrections, and source leads.
Review loop — published records remain correctable; community members may submit updates as new evidence appears.

Privacy and Safety Rules

Do not publish private phone numbers, private email addresses, home addresses, private spreadsheets, or internal administration links.
Treat family history, immigration stories, political history, church records, and elder testimony with consent-aware care.
Prefer public source links, official documents, and contributor-approved material.
If a person asks for a correction or removal of sensitive information, route it through the Echopedia correction process.
